text: DECISION: keep gate and commit optional rather than merging them into done, because they are useful checkpoints on long units but a short unit should need only brief, judge and done
DECISION: upgrade the repo's vendored runtime only between certified units, so a unit is never judged by the code it changes

DECISION: a fake AWS key in tests/e2e.py halted the first done. It is a true detection of a false positive. Assembled the key at runtime in the tests, and added exact file: rule grants so a person can excuse a real false positive; broad secret grants stay refused
CORRECTION: the runtime was upgraded and a second unit opened before the first unit was certified. Both units are now judged together on one tree rather than pretending they were separate

what: Round 1 blind panel scored 7.5 weighted (8.5, 6.8, 7.3, 7.5); 9.5 is the bar
why: recorded before any fix so the improvement can be judged against the real starting point

what: Quarantined tests stay visible in baseline.json and warn on every gate and receipt, instead of leaving the baseline
why: the messy-adoption panelist reproduced a silent drop followed by a permanently broken test passing

what: Node, Go and Rust get per-test ratchets through one regex probe
why: one red test at baseline otherwise left a language with no protection at all, and a single probe covers them without per-language code

what: A unit needs an explicit proof; a proof of true is flagged in its receipt
why: a forgotten proof silently certified a claim of proof

what: A saturated chain stage cannot be reopened with chain start; a person runs unit reopen
why: chain start --reopen silently reset the attempt budget

what: Grants must match lines the gate printed
why: a grant on a file path was accepted, did nothing, and pushed agents toward a broad pattern

what: Reject an in-place assertion edit, but ignore comment-only edits
why: a rename and a weakened assertion look the same to a line diff, so strictness stays and the docs say a grant is needed

what: Self-judging needs one sample
why: repeating the same judge adds no independence and dead-ended after one failure

what: Land --merge gates the combination carrying the stages' grants
why: the earlier fallback lost those grants and could be misreported as a moved branch

what: Skill stays a named binding recorded in the receipt, not a new mechanism
why: native agents define capabilities; a harness that re-implemented them would be over-engineering

what: Round 2 blind panel scored 8.1 weighted (8.5, 7.4, 8.65, 7.85)
why: fresh evaluators on the fixed build; still short of 9.5

what: A test failing anywhere under a name counts as not passing
why: same-named tests in another Go package or Node file hid regressions

what: Quarantine is sticky for five straight passing commits
why: one pass re-armed the veto and produced intermittent false rejects

what: Failed gates cost nothing; only a failed commit, brief or done costs an attempt
why: probing with gate could saturate a unit in minutes, and frontier models iterate far more than this assumed

what: A failed evaluator cannot re-judge the same tree
why: otherwise the retry rule could be sidestepped by asking the same evaluator again

what: Self-judging stays one sample and the docs say so
why: repeating the same judge adds no independence; three failures still halt the unit

what: Assertions in tests that were never green are exempt from the weakening scan, but edited assertions in green tests still need a grant
why: fixing a test that was wrong is the honest path; a line diff cannot tell strengthening from weakening, so the safe side stays strict

what: Lint ratchet only when the project configures ruff
why: an unconfigured linter vetoed a first edit in projects that never asked for it

what: Did not implement scope checks against the unit's base commit
why: that case needs a deliberate --no-verify, and chain integration already catches it

what: Did not add required brief before judge
why: it would add a step without catching a defect

what: Round 3 panel so far 9.05, 8.4, 8.05
why: architect's score pending; recorded as received

what: A new failing test now fails the gate, tracked through a red list rather than a new check
why: the messy panelist certified a unit that had added a red test; a red-count check would have run the suite twice

what: Node runs the project's own test script with the TAP reporter
why: ignoring it left tests in non-default paths unprotected

what: A pytest proof fails only when its summary shows nothing passed
why: trusting exit codes alone missed skip-only proofs, and requiring a summary falsely failed quiet configurations

what: A proof inside a chain stage is changed in the chain file
why: integration re-runs the chain's proof, so changing only the unit made a sound stage fail

what: Pre-commit hook restores itself on first use in a clone
why: hooks do not travel with git, and a new machine silently lost the gate

what: Planned units take their diff base when the previous unit finishes
why: every pre-planned unit otherwise reported the whole history as its own change

what: Round 3 blind panel scored 8.35 weighted (9.05, 8.05, 8.4, 7.9)
why: recorded before fixes; progression is 7.5, 8.1, 8.35

what: Do not flag every edited line in a green test, but do flag edited uppercase test constants
why: the architect's change of an expected value slipped through; a blanket rule would veto ordinary test maintenance

what: A secret-shaped assignment in a test file is not a hard stop; real key formats still are
why: a test fixture password froze a whole chain

what: Documented that evaluator independence is a protocol
why: the runtime cannot verify who ran judge; claiming otherwise would be false

what: Chain nesting does not depend on subagents nesting
why: chains nest through worktrees, so the doc should not claim anything about subagent depth

what: Round 4 blind panel scored 8.51 weighted (9.15, 8.15, 8.7, 8.05)
why: recorded before fixes; progression is 7.5, 8.1, 8.35, 8.51

what: Stop after one more full panel round and report the real score
why: the curve is flattening and each panel now finds narrower edge cases; continuing indefinitely would turn into the over-engineering the owner ruled out

what: A reopened stage keeps its own committed tests protected
why: two panelists gutted their own test after reopen and the docs said a grant was needed

what: Replace the Edit and Write hook with native permissions.deny rules
why: the architect noted native rules are enforced by Claude Code while a regex hook is best effort

what: Grants on a none check must include the printed text after the file name
why: a file-wide pattern excused every later weakening in that unit

what: Leave --unit - commits unscoped
why: that is its purpose, for files outside any unit such as a chain file; the receipt records what was touched

what: Keep four flake runs
why: two would turn real flakes into false rejects, and a failing gate should not be the fast path

what: Do not qualify Go test names by package
why: a test failing anywhere under a name already counts as not passing; the residual case needs a package to fail to build while a same-named test passes elsewhere

what: Round 5 blind panel scored 8.6 weighted (8.4, 8.85, 9.05, 8.1); the 9.5 target was not reached
why: the score is reported as measured; progression is 7.53, 8.1, 8.35, 8.51, 8.6

what: Stop the rounds here, and fix only what certifies something false or misstates behaviour
why: gains have slowed to about 0.1 per round while each panel finds narrower edge cases; pushing further would add machinery the owner has ruled out

what: Fixes made after round 5 were not re-scored
why: a score must come from evaluators, and no panel has seen this exact build

what: Chain grants obey the same rules as command-line grants
why: a bare star in a chain file landed deleted tests without any person being asked

what: Untracked Python files count toward public_api
why: new symbols were unprotected until the commit after they were added

what: Keep unit reopen resetting attempts
why: it requires a person in Claude Code, is logged, and is recorded in the receipt

what: Do not add per-test AST hashing for weakening
why: a semantic check is a project of its own; documented as a limit

what: Restored the original chain fixture line in the test instead of granting an exception
why: the harness flagged my own edit, and there was a way to make the change without weakening anything, so no grant was needed

note: grant tests --allow 'lost: *' (or 'new failure: *') bypasses the bare-star guard and stores allow=['*'], excusing every lost test; the exact 'new failure: X' line the gate prints cannot be granted at all; build-cache e2e check passes with the exclusion removed, two ck(..., True) checks, and quarantine visibility has no test

what: The final evaluator failed the unit; fixed its findings rather than arguing with the score
why: a bare star could still slip through a grant prefix, and several tests would have passed with the feature removed

what: When every test fails, name the losses instead of saying the suite did not run
why: the veto held either way, but an agent told 'did not run' goes looking for a broken toolchain instead of its own regression

note: acceptance: the bare-star fix is a literal check; ?* and "*: *" pass CLI grant and chain typecheck and land deleted tests unasked; reopening an integrated stage loses certified work at land; land --merge skips stage proofs/checks and drops uncommitted log on failure
test_honesty: removing the secret hash suffix, the grant must-match rule or the land --merge gate leaves every e2e check green; three goal items have tests that cannot fail

why: judges

what: Reversed the never-green exemption: rewriting or deleting a red test's assertions needs a named grant
why: the owner spotted it on the explainer; reproduced: assert True passed the gate and entered the baseline as green, and the exemption's own test did exactly that

what: Committed at the owner's request with unit polish still open; two fresh evaluators failed it
why: the owner chose to stop and test this version; the deterministic gate is green, the verdicts stand as failed, and the reproduced defects are listed as open rather than scored over
